newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan tea prices fall on bigger volumes.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan tea prices fall on bigger volumes.

text.p: Sri Lankan tea prices fell all around at the Colombo auction as selective buyers awaited larger quantities seen coming on the market, brokers said.
"There's a lot more tea in the market right now," said a broker. "As a result buyers can be selective. There's no rush to pick up whatever tea there is.
"This trend should continue for the next two or three sales and then stabilise," he added.
Brokers Forbes and Walker said the anticipated gross auction average fell to 118 rupees ($2.07) per kg for the 5.2 million kg on offer against 120.70 rupees last week.
Wednesday's price dip broke a pattern in which tea prices had been soaring in recent months on a combination of higher demand and lower quantities.
Prices peaked at the October 16 auction when the weekly average price hit an all-time high of 124.08 rupees, surpassing the previous week's record 123.71 rupees, brokers said.
The next auction is on November 5-6 where 5.3 million kg will be on offer.
